public_rationale: OpenAI's own exam table shows an uneven profile. GPT-4 scored near the 89th percentile on SAT Math and earned top AP scores. But it scored in the 6th–12th percentile on the AMC 10 high-school math competition and below the 5th percentile on Codeforces programming contests. Aschenbrenner, who made the comparison, admits GPT-4 is much better than smart high schoolers on some tasks and cannot do others. Strong on some tasks and weak on others is what Marcus described, so GPT-4 was not equivalent to a smart high schooler on the plain reading. The verdict rests on reading 'equivalent' as a broad match. Aschenbrenner only claimed a rough match.
limitations: 'Equivalent' is undefined; a loose 'roughly comparable' reading could favour Aschenbrenner.
Exam percentiles compare against all test-takers, not only smart students.
The real-world job examples cannot be scored.

statement.excerpt: GPT-4 is not actually equivalent to a smart high schooler.

from_speaker: GPT-4 is not actually equivalent to a smart high schooler
It can do some things better, some worse, very few reliably
our_interpretation: Plain reading: GPT-4's abilities do not match those of a smart high school student across the board. Its profile is uneven, clearly above such a student on some tasks and clearly below on others, so the two are not equivalent.
The claim answers Aschenbrenner's label 'GPT-4 (2023) ~ smart high schooler'. The period is GPT-4's release (March 2023) up to the post date.
Benchmark exam results against human test-takers are used as the main measure. Real-world jobs such as lifeguarding are not scored, because no source measures them.
criteria.support_condition: Published evaluations show GPT-4 well below typical capable high school test-takers on some high-school-level tasks, and not reliable, even if it is above them on others.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Published evaluations show GPT-4 at or above smart-high-schooler level across the range of high-school-level academic and practical tasks, with no clear areas of weakness.

evidence.explanation: On the AMC 10, a high-school math competition, GPT-4 scored in the 6th–12th percentile of test-takers. That is far below a strong high school student.
On competitive programming, GPT-4 ranked below the 5th percentile. This is a clear area where it fell below capable students.

evidence.excerpt: even GPT-4 is still somewhat uneven; for some tasks it’s much better than smart high-schoolers, while there are other tasks it can’t yet do.
evidence.locator: Section 'GPT-2 to GPT-4', paragraph after the SAT/AP remark
evidence.explanation: The author of the comparison himself says GPT-4 is better on some tasks and unable to do others. That matches Marcus's 'some things better, some worse'.
On standard tests like the SAT, GPT-4 scored around the 89th percentile, comparable to a strong high school student. This is the main evidence for the comparison Marcus rejects.
